title: EN16931 Semantic JSON edition upgrade mapping
description: Format of the upgrade mapping files under model/, for example model/en16931/upgrade-2017-2026.json. A mapping states how the paths and the structural facts of one edition of a model relate to those of another, as data: the upgrade command and any binding read it, and nothing about a mapping is written in code. It is not a registry and no validator reads it. It carries no normative prose of either edition, and it authorises no tool to change a value: openPoints names what an upgrade cannot decide on its own.

format.description: Fixed format marker of an ESJ upgrade mapping file.

version.description: Version of the mapping file format, not of either described edition.

model.description: Short token of the model both editions belong to. A mapping never crosses models.

license.description: SPDX identifier of the licence of this file.

notice.description: Attribution and licensing statement for the described standards.

generated.description: Date the file was generated, as YYYY-MM-DD.

sourceStatement.description: How the content of this file was derived and cross-checked.

pathRewrites.description: Every path of the source edition that is not also a path of the target edition, and no other. A term that keeps its path is not listed.

cardinalityChanges.description: Terms whose declared cardinality differs between the two editions.

datatypeChanges.description: Terms whose semantic data type differs between the two editions.

componentChanges.description: Supplementary components a term gains, loses or declares with another cardinality in the target edition.

addedTerms.description: Terms and groups the target edition has and the source edition does not.

renamedTerms.description: Terms whose name differs between the two editions. A name is not carried in a document, so a rename moves no value; it is listed because a register, a renderer or a generated API prints it.

removedTerms.description: Identifiers the source edition has and the target edition does not. A value at one of them has no address in the target edition.

openPoints.description: What an upgrade cannot decide on its own. Every entry is reported and none is repaired: a tool that invents a value to satisfy a new rule has changed an invoice.

reverse.description: What the downgrade does with content the source edition cannot hold.

termId.description: A business term or business group identifier.

path.description: Identifiers from the invoice root down to and including the term, without occurrence indices: the index of a segment follows from the registry of the edition (specification, section 5.3).

edition.description: One end of the mapping: the edition string of its registry, and the same string as a document writes it in semanticModel.

change.description: "moved" where the term hangs under another parent, "index-added" where the chain of identifiers is the same and the path still differs because the term became repeatable and its segment now carries an occurrence index.

allOf.description: An index-added entry changes no identifier chain; that is what distinguishes it from a move.

note.description: What the change does to a value written under the source edition.

rule.description: The business rule of the target edition that the tightening serves, where it names one.

mandatoryInside.description: The group this term is mandatory in. An upgraded document needs a value for it only where that group is present.

parentOptional.description: Whether that group is itself optional. Where it is, a document of the source edition stays complete without the new term.

slug.description: The name stem the target registry gives the term. A term that exists in both editions keeps the stem of the older one, so this member is here to be read rather than to be acted on.

caseOnly.description: Whether the two names differ in letter case alone.

terms.description: The terms the point is about. An empty array means it is about any term the statement fits.

behaviour.description: What the upgrade does. Only "report" is defined: nothing is repaired and nothing is rounded.
